newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Ranbaxy to merge with Croslands.
newsitem.headline: India's Ranbaxy to merge with Croslands.

text.p: Leading Indian pharmaceutical maker Ranbaxy Laboratories Ltd said on Monday it would merge with niche player Croslands Research Laboratories Ltd.
A Ranbaxy spokeswoman said the exchange ratio, approved by Ranbaxy's board on Monday, would be three Ranbaxy shares for seven shares of Croslands.
She said the two firms were scheduled to hold a joint news conference in Bombay on Tuesday to reveal details of the merger.

Analysts said the merger of the smaller niche player into Ranbaxy would benefit both firms. Croslands specialises in skin-care drugs, while Ranbaxy, India's third largest pharmaceutical firm, leads in antibiotics.

"This (the merger) would allow Ranbaxy to enter the high-growth niche therapeutic area of dermatology where Croslands is strong," said Tarun Jaitly, analyst at securities firm James Capel B&K in Bombay.
"Croslands shareholders have also got a good deal," he said.
He said Croslands' strong marketing network would be an asset to Ranbaxy, which is India's third largest pharmaceutical firm after Glaxo-Wellcome India and Cipla.
"The merger is beneficial to Ranbaxy in the long run as it will help expansion of its therapeutic range of products," said Alroy Lobo, pharmaceutical industry analyst at Bombay's Kotak Securities.
"Croslands, with a domestic market share of 0.9 percent, will help Ranbaxy to jump into the second position with a total market share of 4.7 percent," he said.
Analysts said the combined turnover of both firms for the financial year ending March 31, 1997 is expected to be around 11.5 billion rupees against 9.6 billion in 1995/96 (April-March).
Croslands shares jumped 13 rupees, or 5.4 percent, to end at 253.0 on the Bombay Stock Exchange ahead of the announcement. Ranbaxy closed 8.75 rupees or 1.5 percent higher at 605.0.
In another move to consolidate its market position, Ranbaxy also said in a statement received on Monday that it had acquired several well-known brands of Bombay-based Gufic Group.
